intro.lead: Seven questions about your use case. At the end you'll know whether you need an agent or a script will do.
intro.lead.how: This test calls no model. It's one sum and four rules.
intro.privacy: no cookies · your answers stay in your browser

wizard.kbd: arrows to choose · enter to confirm
wizard.error.none: No answer selected. Pick one to continue.
wizard.note.label: Note
wizard.q1.title: What does the input look like?
wizard.q1.hint: Whatever enters the flow on each run.
wizard.q1.a.label: Always structured
wizard.q1.b.label: Mixed
wizard.q1.c.label: Free text
wizard.q2.title: What does the output look like?
wizard.q2.hint: What the flow produces at the end.
wizard.q2.a.label: Fixed template, few variables
wizard.q2.b.label: Template with some free parts
wizard.q2.b.hint: a sentence or two to write
wizard.q2.c.label: Different every time
wizard.q3.title: Are the steps always the same?
wizard.q3.hint: The sequence of operations from input to output.
wizard.q3.a.label: Yes, always
wizard.q3.b.label: A few predictable branches
wizard.q3.c.label: They change based on what it finds
wizard.q4.title: Does it need judgement?
wizard.q4.a.label: No
wizard.q4.b.label: In one spot only
wizard.q4.b.hint: one step, the rest is mechanical
wizard.q4.c.label: Through most of the flow
wizard.q4.c.hint: almost every step needs a decision
wizard.q5.title: How often does it run?
wizard.q5.a.label: Hundreds of times a day
wizard.q5.b.label: Daily
wizard.q5.c.label: Once or rarely
wizard.q6.title: How costly is a wrong output?
wizard.q6.hint: Picture it going out wrong with nobody noticing right away.
wizard.q6.a.label: A lot
wizard.q6.a.hint: needs determinism or an audit trail
wizard.q6.b.label: Somewhat
wizard.q6.c.label: Not much
wizard.q7.title: Does the service have an API or a CLI?
wizard.q7.hint: The system you read from or act on.
wizard.q7.a.label: Yes
wizard.q7.b.label: Only via MCP
wizard.q7.b.hint: I reach it through an MCP server
wizard.q7.c.label: Only via browser or UI
wizard.q7.b.note: Almost every MCP server wraps an API you can call with fetch. Worth a look at what's underneath.
